threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused trying to figure out the bus stops—it's a rite of passage to miss that first double-decker on Clapton Road.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the bus with old reggae tunes. Even the driver was smiling. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I sat in a café on Weserstrasse and heard a heated debate between a Turkish grandmother and a hipster about the best döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop where the meat is grilled to order while locals debate philosophy over their 3am currywurst.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a true local when they know the exact taco truck that serves the only al pastor worth it at 2 am, no google maps needed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a rider singing opera on the 30 Stockton last night. Most of the crowd looked annoyed, but a few were vibing along. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just a trendy spot, but they miss the quiet corners where locals sip café amb llet in peace, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand out with their maps in hand, trying to navigate the labyrinthine streets after dark, completely unaware of the shortcuts locals use.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground' when you're hopping from Dalston Junction to Hackney Central. It’s a tell.
Heard a bloke on the 37 bragging about his collection of 'rare' train tickets. Only in Brixton at 2 AM, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the old guy with a parrot on his shoulder arguing with a street musician about who plays better tunes on Hermannplatz.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Ever noticed how the kebab shops here stay open til dawn? It's like the unofficial after-party scene, with everyone sharing a late-night döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals can tell you which taco truck is worth the wait and which is just Instagram bait. The scent of al pastor is the ultimate test.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 bus today, and a musician was belting out 'California Dreamin''—totally drowned out the engine noises. Classic San Francisco vibe on a dreary day.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the side streets with old workshops that tell the real story of this neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look for a parking spot when they see a bike lane—like it's an unfamiliar landscape.
